statement: Dense Disjoint Grade Layers and Limit-Compatibility Audit: For dilation scale tau = 2*pi and discrete grade layers L_K = tau^K * Z (K in Z), the layer union S_tau = Union_{K in Z} L_K is countable and dense in R, and S_tau^+ = Union_{K in Z} L_K^+ (L_K^+ = tau^K * N_{>0}) is dense in R_{>0}, while distinct integer layers remain arithmetically separated (L_K cap L_J = {0} and L_K^+ cap L_J^+ = empty set for K != J) by the transcendence of 2*pi (Lindemann 1882). When continuous prime-zeta observables are transported along competing grade sequences x_r = n_r * tau^{K_r} -> x and y_r = m_r * tau^{J_r} -> x (K_r != J_r, K_r -> -infty), the correctly converted intrinsic Dirichlet characters A_K^raw = tau^{-Ks} * A_K^int and zero modes satisfy lim_{r -> infty} [A(x_r) - A(y_r)] = 0 identically for all complex frequencies s and zero displacements delta in R. Centered zero modes x^rho / rho are smooth continuous functions of the external coordinate x in (0, infty) for every rho = 1/2 + delta + i*gamma, ensuring that the limit is strictly sequence-independent and grade-compatible for both on-line (delta = 0) and off-line (delta != 0) zeros. Raw pointwise Chebyshev evaluation psi(tau^{-K}X) diverges as K -> -infty and is withdrawn from pointwise limit claims pending Jacobian-normalized measure analysis in Cycle 10. Lean formalizes nu_K multiplicativity under transported multiplication, the exact identity between raw and converted Dirichlet summands, the rational characterization of layer coincidence, and the constructive nearest-integer lattice approximation error bound |x - n*Delta| <= Delta/2 under Mathlib foundational axioms. Therefore, while layer density ensures uniqueness of continuous extension to R_{>0}, the limit-compatibility bridge for continuous observables produces no grade-limit defect and does not distinguish on-line from off-line zeros: transcendental continuation via dense disjoint layers does not provide an exclusion mechanism.

quantified_variables.name: J
quantified_variables.description: Second discrete grade index in Z

quantified_variables.name: delta
quantified_variables.description: Real displacement of zero from critical line

hypotheses: S_tau = Union_{K in Z} tau^K * Z is dense in R
S_tau^+ = Union_{K in Z} tau^K * N_{>0} is dense in R_{>0}
iota_K(n) = tau^K * n embeds N_{>0} into L_K^+
nu_K(x) = x / tau^K is the intrinsic unit-reading map
chi_{K,s}(x) = nu_K(x)^{-s} is the transported Dirichlet character
object_studied: Dense disjoint layer union S_tau^+, competing grade sequences x_r and y_r, and limit compatibility of converted observables and zero modes
fourier_normalization: Additive Fourier-Laplace transform on R; Mellin transform on R_+
multiplicity_convention: Nontrivial zero multiplicity m_rho >= 1 and discrete grade indexing K, J in Z
measure_and_window: Counting measure on discrete layers L_K^+; Lebesgue measure dx on R_+
order_of_limits: Grade index limit K_r, J_r -> -infty; point convergence x_r, y_r -> x > 0
exact_conclusion: The layer union is dense and its constituent layers are arithmetically separated. Correct unit conversion makes the tested prime-zeta observables restrictions of ordinary continuous functions of the external coordinate for every rho. Density therefore gives uniqueness of continuation but does not produce any grade-limit defect for delta != 0.
logical_negation: The union S_tau fails to be dense, or integer layers intersect at non-zero points, or correctly converted zero modes exhibit a grade-limit defect distinguishing delta != 0 from delta = 0 (FALSIFIED / REFUTED)
falsification_attempts: Gate 1 & 4 (Symbolic Elimination & Equality-Case Audit): performed equality-case analysis on m * tau^K = n * tau^J, proving that non-zero solutions are impossible for K != J by Lindemann (1882) and that equality holds only at the trivial zero m = n = 0; cancellation analysis on competing sequences proves that the converted character defect A(x_r) - A(y_r) vanishes identically in the limit

Gate 2 & 5 (Boundary Dominance & Intrinsic vs Raw Unit Conversion): verified that intrinsic character chi_{K,s}(x) = nu_K(x)^{-s} = n^{-s} and raw Dirichlet kernel (n*tau^K)^{-s} differ by exact non-vanishing unit factor tau^{-Ks}, with asymptotic boundary limit K -> -infty decaying for Re(s) > 0; both preserve zero divisor

Gate 3 & 9 (Limit-Compatibility & Defect Testing): tested Candidates 1-5 along competing disjoint grade sequences x_r in L_{-r}^+ and y_r in L_{-(2r+1)}^+; proved lim [A(x_r) - A(y_r)] = 0 for raw Dirichlet kernel, converted character, and zero modes

Gate 6 & 7 (Zero Mode Continuity & Delta Independence): tracked complex phase and modulus of centered zero modes x^lambda (lambda = delta + i*gamma); proved that continuity on (0, infty) holds identically for both on-line (delta = 0) and off-line (delta != 0) zeros, refuting the hypothesis that off-line zeros produce a grade-limit defect
Gate 8 (Non-Circularity Audit): audited results without assuming RH, temperedness, or polynomial bounds, proving unconditionally that limit compatibility fails to provide an exclusion mechanism
Gate 10 (Dual Status Classification): passed all structural schema gates and established formal epistemic bounds in Lean and Python
